findings.summary: Some dimension-to-field mappings use metadata fields that are almost always set, so the function overstates coverage
findings.evidence: 'validation' counts as filled whenever `record.evidence.is_some()`. introspect.rs:1396 sets evidence on every run where the model returned, including runs whose outcome is a failure, so a failed introspection still reports 'validation'. In the same way, 'scope' is just `intervention.is_some()`, which is a link set whenever an intervention triggered the run (line 1322), and 'escape' is just prevention_kind. A more honest version would map only the fields that actually carry a dimension's content and report the dimensions the record cannot hold (validation, scope) as never filled, or say so in the doc comment and the spec measure. The accepted reading let the producer adjust the mapping and ruled out schema changes, so I rate this minor.

findings.summary: Nothing calls the new function yet
findings.evidence: A Grep finds filled_feedback_dimensions only in its definition, its test, the spec and the changelog. summary: This change passes. It adds `filled_feedback_dimensions` and `FEEDBACK_DIMENSIONS` to `crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs`, records the function as OLY-3-05's mechanism in `docs/spec.toml` with owner "Athena", and writes a measure that names the test and ends with `status: not shown`. The new test passed when I ran `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`. It would fail if the function returned an empty set or any fixed set. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed, and I did not rerun the full suite. The diff stays within the expected deliverables. The changelog entry sits under Unreleased → Added. There are two minor issues. First, some dimensions are filled from metadata that is almost always set: "validation" counts whenever the model ran, even if the run failed, and "scope" counts whenever an intervention triggered the run. Second, nothing calls the function yet. The accepted reading allowed both, so neither fails the change.
